review.material: The complete publisher abstract for the 2018 chapter was read. A related 2017 author-linked URL returned a website page instead of its PDF, and was not treated as the chapter text.
review.limitations: The kolam rules and comparative computations were not inspected. The 2017 presentation and 2018 chapter are not asserted to be identical.

evidence.description: Primary abstract of the published 2018 chapter.

sections.title: What it is about
sections.text: Knight examines craft as performance in time, using traditional Indian kolam pattern making. The focus is on how making unfolds, alongside the design left behind.

sections.title: Premise
sections.text: Can grammars represent temporal actions and the social, aesthetic or creative importance of performance, rather than treating process merely as a way to obtain a product?

sections.title: Method reported
sections.text: The chapter compares making grammars for craft performance with shape grammars for craft designs through the kolam case. It is a conceptual comparison, not a controlled experiment.

sections.title: Reported conclusion
sections.text: The abstract says the comparison reveals different generative strategies. It does not give enough detail to reconstruct those strategies here.

sections.title: Reading boundary
sections.text: Full-text rules, case selection and supporting discussion remain unreviewed. The abstract does not establish a universal model of every kolam maker’s practice.

sections.title: Why follow the original
sections.text: A final pattern does not record every action that made it. Look for what changes when you describe both material configuration and the maker’s sequence of actions.

terms.meaning: The Indian pattern-making craft used as this chapter’s case study.
The embodied, temporal activity of making, distinguished from only its final artifact.
